title: Europe’s Public Investment Boom Changes Shape
gist: The EU's NextGenerationEU program is winding down, but aggregate EU government investment is still expected to hold near 4% of GDP in 2027; the real story is compositional — a rotation from civilian to defense spending and a shift in the marginal investment impulse from Southern/Eastern Europe toward Germany and Northern Europe.

themes.theme: No investment cliff, but a rotation

insights.claim: Even though the European Union's post-Covid NextGenerationEU investment program is approaching its expiry, EU government investment is expected to stay close to 4% of GDP in 2027.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Fade the consensus 'EU fiscal investment cliff' trade at the aggregate level; the headline capex level holds even as the funding source changes.
insights.quote: Yet EU government investment is expected to stay close to 4% of GDP in 2027.
insights.locator: The European Union’s post-Covid investment program

insights.claim: Stable headline EU public investment masks two shifts: a rotation from civilian to defense investment, and a move in the marginal investment impulse toward Germany and Northern Europe.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Favor European defense-linked industrials and German/Nordic domestic capex beneficiaries over civilian-infrastructure names levered to periphery EU grants.
insights.quote: This apparent stability masks a rotation from civilian to defense investment and a geographical shift in the marginal investment impulse toward Germany and Northern Europe.
insights.locator: This apparent stability masks a rotation

insights.claim: Southern and Eastern Europe were the main beneficiaries of the expiring EU program, so the end of the funding poses a localized investment cliff risk there even if the EU aggregate holds up.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Watch peripheral and CEE growth, construction and credit exposures for a downshift that won't show up in EU-wide investment data.
insights.quote: At first glance, its expiry threatens an investment cliff, particularly in Southern and Eastern Europe, the program’s main beneficiaries
insights.locator: At first glance, its expiry threatens

insights.claim: The Recovery and Resilience Facility accounts for roughly 90% of NextGenerationEU funds, and of the €575bn earmarked for spending only about €310bn had been recorded by the end of 2025.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Roughly €265bn of earmarked funds remained unrecorded entering 2026, implying a use-it-or-lose-it disbursement rush that front-loads activity before the program ends.
insights.quote: Of the €575bn earmarked for spending, around €310bn had been recorded by the end of 2025.

insights.claim: EU government gross fixed capital formation rose from €469bn to €727bn between 2021 and 2025, and Recovery and Resilience Facility funds drove roughly 40% of that increase.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Quantifies how much of Europe's public capex boom was EU-grant-financed rather than nationally funded — the share that must be replaced by national or defense budgets.
insights.quote: These funds drove roughly 40% of the rise in government gross fixed capital formation
insights.locator: These funds drove roughly 40% of the rise

insights.claim: Southern and Eastern Europe generated 86% of the 2021-2025 rise in EU government gross fixed capital formation despite accounting for just 37% of EU GDP.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The extreme concentration means the coming geographic rotation is a large relative-growth swing factor for periphery versus core European assets.
insights.quote: The surge was concentrated in Southern and Eastern Europe, which generated 86% of the rise despite accounting for just 37% of EU GDP.
